findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The Quaternary ammonium sanitizer dispenser is observed to be dispensing at a concentration of 0ppm. The PIC made sanitizer using the bottle during the inspection and it tested to be at 400 ppm. A follow up is scheduled for 10/8/26 to ensure that the sanitizer dispenser is repaired and is sanitizing at a labeled-recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There were cutting boards observed to be stored behind the prep sink faucet. Faucets are not clean, sanitized surfaces and can expose food-contact surfaces to contamination. CORRECTED - The cutting boards were removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. The cutting boards will be stored on the clean dish shelves moving forward. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are stored in a manner that protects them from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The inspectors observed a small gap on the lower right edge of the back door. Gaps in outer openings of the facility may allow for the entry of pests. Ensure that this gap is weather stripped or sealed by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: There are observed to be nitrile gloves, foam cups, and lids stored in the women’s restroom that currently is out of order. CORRECTED- The PIC removed these items from the restroom. Ensure that single-service articles and utensils are never stored in a toilet room.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(2) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT,UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (2) In toilet rooms.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The inspectors observed rust along the shelves of the standing cooler towards the back of the store. Nonfood contact surfaces should be free of rust and any debris that may pose a potential to contaminate food items. Ensure shelves are replaced, or cleaned and repainted by the next routine inspection to have a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: The ice bin was observed to be stored in ready to use position with the food contact surface facing upwards. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) inverted the ice bin. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored in a position to prevent contamination.

(B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No measurable concentration of quat sanitizer was observed in the sanitizer buckets or 3 compartment sink. The sanitizer concentrate jug was completely empty and no sanitizer was observed in the feeder hose to the wall-mounted dispenser. CORRECTED- PIC replaced the concentrate jug and ran the wall-mounted dispenser until sanitizer was flowing. Sanitizer solutions were observed at 200ppm quat. Clean dishes were re-sanitized and set aside to air-dry. Discuss test strip use and checking the concentrate jug and hose when dispensing sanitizer solution.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label (200-400ppm), and water with 500ppm hardness or less. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: There is no ambient thermometer present in the 3 door cooler. CORRECTED- A thermometer was moved from the walk-in freezer to the 3 door cooler. Ensure thermometers are placed in all cold holding units.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following areas of the facility are in disrepair:
- Tile on the floor to the left of the triple sink (under the backup chemical shelf) is damaged and peeling away from the floor
- Spray foam has been used to fill the missing tile around a pipe in the wall to the left of the triple sink. Paint or otherwise seal the spray foam is it is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Two wet mops were observed piled in the mop sink/mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, who hung the mops to air-dry using the wall-mounted hanger. Ensure mop water is discarded immediately after use, and that mops are stored after use in a way that will allow them to air dry.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
3rd REPEAT: Food handler certificates are not available in the facility for review during inspection. PIC indicated that food handler training is typically completed upon hiring, and that certificates are stored on the computer. Ensure that all employees have current food handler certificates on file and available for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
